role.altitude: The skincare specialist keeps examining skin, treating, advising and working with doctors; paper client cards, referral notes and sorting supplier mail shrink.
skills_to_grow: Keeping client cards complete with consent recorded
role.ambitious_version: A specialist whose notes and photos let a doctor see a client's progress at a glance.

tasks.short: Read trade news and supplier newsletters, attend trainings and fairs, check claims of new products, and share what is new with colleagues.

steps.what: Skincare specialist reads trade magazines, supplier newsletters and posts to stay abreast of the latest industry trends, products and treatments

loop.input: Supplier newsletters and trade mails arriving in the specialist's work mailbox during the week.
loop.output: A weekly list of new products, treatments and research items, one line each with a link to the source mail or page.
loop.check: Every line must link to the mail or page it came from and repeat its title, or it is dropped. The specialist reads each line they might act on against its source and drops lines whose summary does not match what the source says; anything acted on is read in full at the source.
loop.why_not_simpler: A mail filter sorts senders but cannot pull out which of many items are new.

steps.what: Skincare specialist attends supplier trainings, fairs and webinars
Skincare specialist checks the claims and ingredient lists of new products
Skincare specialist shares what is new with colleagues in the team meeting

tasks.design: A bounded step turns the week's supplier newsletters and trade mails into one list of new items, each linked to its source, so the specialist skims one page instead of many mails. Trainings, judging product claims and sharing with colleagues stay as they are.
tasks.previous_blocker: News arrived in many separate mails mixed with promotions.
tasks.enabler_now: Language models can list items from mails with a link to each source.
tasks.still_hard: Judging which new treatment is real progress and which is marketing.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing from experience which claims to doubt.
tasks.altitude: Little changes; reading takes less time.

reach.learn: Which new items the team asks about.

evidence.claim: Language models can list items from a batch of mails with a link to each source.
No AI Act high-risk area covers reading trade news.

assumptions: Boundary: keeping up with the field; buying products is outside.
Input contract for s1: newsletters and trade mails in the specialist's work mailbox; social media posts are still read by hand.
Trainings, assessment and sharing keep their full time.
unknowns: How many newsletters arrive per week.
research_questions: Does the specialist miss items that are not in the list?

already_counted.description: Skincare specialist opens sources behind list items worth acting on.

incremental.description: Skincare specialist keeps the newsletter subscriptions tidy.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: a few trusted newsletters and many social posts read by hand, so the list saves little and s1 keeps 90 (3.7); high: many suppliers mailing weekly (9.7).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Spot a possible serious skin problem, explain it to the client and refer them to medical personnel, note it on the client card and give a note for the doctor.

steps.what: Skincare specialist spots a possible serious skin problem during intake or treatment
Client gives explicit consent on the intake form for health notes and photos
Skincare specialist explains the concern and refers the client to medical personnel for treatment
Skincare specialist notes the observation and advice: on the paper client card today, in fixed fields with a photo on the digital card after the change
Skincare specialist writes a short note for the client to show the doctor: by hand today; printed from the card's fields after the change, with any wording added
Skincare specialist checks the printed note: it says what was seen and advised, nothing more, and carries the client's name
Skincare specialist hands the checked note to the client for the doctor

approvals.approved_version: The note for the doctor exactly as checked by the specialist in s4c, handed once to the client it is about; any change needs a new check.

tasks.design: Spotting the problem and the conversation stay with the specialist. The specialist writes the observation on the client card in the salon system ({OTHER}) with fixed fields and, with the client's explicit consent, a photo, which takes as long as the paper card; a short note for the doctor is printed from those fields, checked and handed to the client to take along. No app or model judges the skin.
tasks.previous_blocker: Observations were on paper cards and notes for doctors handwritten.
tasks.enabler_now: Salon systems hold client cards with notes, photos and signed consent forms.
tasks.still_hard: Telling a client to see a doctor without alarming them.
tasks.human_edge: Recognising a mole that should not wait.

reach.learn: Whether the specialist's note helps the first consult.

evidence.claim: A salon system offers paperless client cards with treatment notes, before-and-after photos and signed digital forms.
Notes on skin conditions are health data; outside a healthcare contract they need the client's explicit consent.

assumptions: Boundary: from spotting the problem to the note handed over; medical care is outside.
Input contract for s4: the observation fields the specialist fills in s3; fallback is a handwritten note.
Photos and notes are kept only with explicit consent recorded on the intake form.

Spotting, the conversation, noting the observation and the check and hand-over keep their full time; the observation is the specialist's own first record. s4 keeps 50 because the note prints from the fields and the specialist adds only what the fields miss. The client's consent is shown as s1c.
research_questions: Do referred clients come back with the doctor's advice?

incremental.description: Skincare specialist records the client's consent for health notes and photos.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: rare referrals where the note needs much wording by hand, so s4 keeps 80 (1.1); high: frequent referrals with standard notes (3.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Receive the doctor's plan, collaborate with plastic surgeons and dermatologists on pre- and postoperative skin care, give the treatments, record progress and report back to the doctor.

steps.what: Skincare specialist receives the referral and treatment plan from the surgeon or dermatologist
Skincare specialist collaborates with the surgeon or dermatologist on the plan
Patient gives explicit consent on the intake form for photos and for sharing progress with the doctor
Skincare specialist provides pre- and postoperative skin care treatments
Skincare specialist records each treatment and the skin's progress with photos: on paper today, in fixed fields on the digital card after the change
Skincare specialist writes the progress report for the doctor: from scratch today; generated from the treatment records after the change, with the specialist's own assessment added
Skincare specialist checks the final report: it matches the treatment records and photos, the patient consented to sharing, and the doctor's secure address
Skincare specialist sends the checked report to the doctor by secure mail

approvals.approved_version: The progress report with records and photos exactly as checked by the specialist in s5c, sent once by secure mail to the referring doctor; any change needs a new check.

tasks.design: The doctor's referral is filed on the client card in the salon system ({OTHER}), and the specialist records each treatment there with fixed fields and photos taken with the client's explicit consent, which takes as long as on paper. The progress report for the doctor is generated from those records, and the specialist checks it and sends it by secure mail. Talks with the doctor and the treatments stay as they are.
tasks.previous_blocker: Progress was noted on paper and reports to doctors were written from scratch.
tasks.enabler_now: Salon systems keep treatment notes with photos and print summaries from them.
tasks.still_hard: Adjusting treatment to how the skin heals.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing early that a scar is healing badly.
tasks.altitude: Little changes; reports take less writing.

reach.learn: Whether photo-based progress reports cut follow-up visits.

evidence.claim: A salon system keeps treatment notes, before-and-after photos and signed digital forms per client.
Skin notes and photos are health data; sharing them with a doctor needs explicit consent and secure mail.

assumptions: Boundary: from the referral to the progress report; surgery is outside.
Input contract for s5: the treatment records and photos the specialist enters in s4; fallback is a written report.
Consent for photos and sharing is recorded on the intake form.

Talks with the doctor, treatments, recording progress and the check and send of the report keep their full time; progress notes are the specialist's own first record. s1 keeps 70 because the referral is filed on the card instead of on paper; s5 keeps 40 because the report fills from the records and the specialist adds the assessment. The patient's consent is shown as s2c.
unknowns: Share of clients referred by doctors.
research_questions: Do doctors read the generated reports?

incremental.description: Skincare specialist records consent for photos and sharing.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few doctor referrals and doctors who want reports in their own format, so s5 keeps 75 (4.5); high: a clinic working with surgeons weekly (7.3).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Look at the client's skin and features, advise clients about colors and types of makeup, instruct them in makeup application techniques and note the chosen products.

steps.what: Skincare specialist looks at the client's skin tone, type and features
Skincare specialist advises clients about colors and types of makeup
Skincare specialist instructs the client in makeup application techniques
Skincare specialist writes the chosen products and colours on the client card

tasks.design: Advice and teaching stay hands-on. Products the client buys are written to the client card in the salon system ({OTHER}) by the checkout, and the specialist adds only colour notes, so the next visit or repurchase starts from the card.
tasks.previous_blocker: Product choices were written on paper cards that were often incomplete.
tasks.enabler_now: Salon checkouts write sold products to the client card.
tasks.still_hard: Everything that makes the advice good.
tasks.human_edge: Choosing colours that suit the client in daylight.

reach.learn: Whether clients reorder the same products from the card.

evidence.claim: Salon client cards hold treatment and purchase history.
Sales records are kept seven years for tax.

assumptions: Boundary: the advice session; selling at the counter is outside.

Input contract for s4: products sold, written to the client card by the salon checkout when the receptionist or specialist rings up the sale, as today; colour notes typed by the specialist; fallback is the paper card.
Coverage: about 70% of clients buy at least one product; for the rest the specialist types the advice.
The session keeps its full time.
unknowns: Share of sessions with a purchase.
research_questions: Do repurchases rise when products are on the card?

incremental.description: No new work beyond the steps: colour notes are part of s4.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: one-off sessions where only about a third of clients buy, so the specialist types most advice and s4 keeps 65 (3.5); high: about 70% buy as assumed (6.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional
